title: Dark Matter
subtitle: The invisible universe

description:
Episode 20 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌑
We hunt dark matter: why galaxies don't fly apart, five times more of it than normal matter, how we see it bend light, the Bullet Cluster, and why everything we can see is just 5% of the universe.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 21: Next stop, dark energy. The force pushing the universe apart.

segments.text: Episode twenty. Next stop... dark matter.
Galaxies spin so fast they should fly apart. Something invisible is holding them together.
segments.headline: Something invisible

segments.text: Scientists call it dark matter. There's about five times more of it than normal matter.

visual.label: more dark matter than normal matter

segments.text: We can't see it or touch it. We only see its gravity, bending the light of distant galaxies.
segments.headline: We only see its gravity

segments.text: This is the Bullet Cluster. Two clusters of galaxies smashed together, and the dark matter, shown in blue, passed right through.
segments.headline: The Bullet Cluster

segments.text: Everything we can see, every star, planet and person, is only about five percent of the universe.

visual.label: of the universe is normal matter

segments.text: Tomorrow, we meet something even stranger, pushing the universe apart. Next stop: dark energy. Follow, so you don't miss episode twenty-one.
